extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, practitioners, and policy analysts searching Federal Register documents about Title IX actions
extracted.subtask_short: federalregister search results for Title IX
extracted.subtask_description: A machine-readable search-results listing of Federal Register documents matching the term 'Title IX', showing metadata (title, type, abstract, document number, urls, publication date, agencies) and short excerpts from each document. Useful for locating rulemaking notices, proposed rules, rescissions, and information-collection notices related to Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) information-collection notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In compliance with the requirement of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, agencies invite the public and other Federal agencies to comment on proposed and/or continuing information collections. OMB will accept comments from the public during its review and approval period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must include OMB Number; Expiration Date of Approval; Type of Review (e.g., extension, revision); Abstract summarizing the proposed information collection; burden estimates (costs and respondent hours); Respondent's Obligation (mandatory/voluntary); Legal Authority; and a Request for Comments period (commonly 30 or 60 days). Example language from the page: 'The proposed information collection is summarized below and describes the nature of the information collection and its expected burden. Public comments on the ICR are invited. OMB will accept comments from the public during this review and approval period.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) meeting notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of meetings for federal advisory committees must be published where required by FACA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states: 'Notice of this meeting is required under section 10(a)(2) of the Federal Advisory Committee Act.' In practice, a meeting notice published in the Federal Register should cite the FACA requirement and provide statutory basis, contact information, and supplementary information about the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of proposed rules must state effective withdrawal date and DATES header
rubrics_metrics.description: When withdrawing a previously published notice of proposed rulemaking, the Federal Register entry must state that the notice 'is withdrawn as of [date]' and include a DATES section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language on the page: 'The notice of proposed rulemaking published in the Federal Register on April 13, 2023, ... is withdrawn as of December 20, 2024.' Include a clear DATES: subsection and FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of guidance — immediate effect and rescinds former guidance in entirety
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency issues a rescission of guidance, it may state that the rescission is effective immediately and that it rescinds the former guidance in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text: 'This rule is effective immediately and rescinds the former guidance in its entirety.' Notices explaining rescissions should include the reasoning (e.g., later court cases, executive orders) and reference the original guidance being rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory amendments must state purpose and alignment with statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations should state their purpose and how they align with the governing statute's nondiscrimination mandate or other statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the page: 'The purpose of these amendments is to better align the Title IX regulatory requirements with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate.' Agencies should explain how amendments clarify scope, recipient obligations, and provide discretion/flexibility as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of publication metadata and access links
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register entries include structured metadata such as document_number, html_url, pdf_url, public_inspection_pdf_url, publication_date, agencies, and abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search-results JSON shows all documents include these fields; rulemaking notices and comments should include accessible URLs to the HTML and PDF, the public-inspection PDF URL, a clear abstract, and agency attribution (name, raw_name, url). Also commonly included: excerpts, contact blocks, and document type (Rule, Proposed Rule, Notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required sections: FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT and SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking and notice documents customarily include 'FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT' and a 'SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION' section that expands on the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page show: 'FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Bianca Costello...' and 'SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: I. Abstract ...' These sections provide contact details, background, statutory discussion, and additional explanation for stakeholders and commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and statutory citations must be provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices and rules must identify the legal authority under which the action is taken, with specific statutory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page excerpts include 'Legal Authority: Section 60305 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021...' and numerous references to 'Title IX', 'Title VI', 'Section 504', etc. Agencies should cite the exact statute or Executive Order authorizing the action and often include a list of authorities at the end of the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant awardees must provide non-discrimination assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain agencies require grant applicants to submit an assurance of non-discrimination as part of the initial grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'NASA ... requires grant awardees to submit an assurance of non-discrimination (NASA Form 1206) as part of their initial grant application.' The page also notes that a recipient's assurance and certification can provide an independent contractual basis for enforcement and may give rise to a False Claims Act violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices should include an abstract or summary describing the action and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Federal Register entry includes an abstract that summarizes the action (e.g., rescission, proposed rule, final rule) and states intended effects or rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: abstracts in the listing describe the nature of the action, such as 'This notice rescinds guidance that defines the term "sex"...' or 'The U.S. Department of Education amends the regulations implementing Title IX...' Abstracts help readers quickly determine relevance and should state what is being changed and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking/Regulatory changes may be framed to conform to statutory text and executive orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may amend or rescind portions of regulations expressly to 'conform more closely with the statutory text' or to implement Executive Orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language: 'rescinding portions ... to conform more closely with the statutory text and to implement Executive Order 14281.' When doing so, documents commonly explain policy goals such as avoiding constitutional concerns, reducing compliance costs, or serving the public interest.
